task_instance: Prepare a small private Python repository (with a leaked API key buried in its git history) for public open-source release, following the skill's workflow: detect org profile, audit history for secrets and decide keep-vs-recreate, run a readiness check, add README/CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY.md/LICENSE/CI, verify licensing consistency, get tests passing, tag a semver release, and verify a clean clone builds and works.
blocker_detail: The skill's own scripts/detect_org.sh and scripts/check_readiness.sh referenced in SKILL.md were not present in this benchmark source checkout (only SKILL.md and LICENSE exist there), so their logic was reimplemented inline in bash rather than run verbatim. Also, the genuinely GitHub-account-bound tail of the workflow (actually flipping repository visibility to public, enabling secret scanning/push protection in repo settings, configuring branch protection/Dependabot, publishing a package via trusted OIDC) was not attempted, since it requires an authenticated GitHub account/paid or account-bound service and public deployment, which the safety rules exclude. This did not block the core deliverable: everything achievable purely on local files/git was done and verified.
evidence: Built /tmp/.../sample-repo: a 3-commit git history where commit a13b106 hardcodes API_KEY = "sk_live_..." and a later commit 059c534 removes it from HEAD but leaves it in history. Ran the skill's Step 1 (detect_org logic) -> printed PROFILE: generic (remote acmecorp/pipeline.git, no trailofbits signal). Ran Step 2 secrets audit: installed detect-secrets via pip and scanned history (it produced a false negative on this pattern), then did the skill-mandated manual history check `git log -p --all | grep sk_live`, which found the secret in 2 diff hunks -- confirming the skill's core teaching point (a scanner alone isn't enough, and a key removed from HEAD is still exposed via history). Per the skill's decision rule (do not rewrite history; recreate the repo instead), created /tmp/.../public-repo as a brand-new git init with only the current tree copied in (no old history), and confirmed a readiness-check style scan of tracked files found no secret patterns. Filled every readiness gap: README.md (what/install/usage/contributing/license sections), CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, .editorconfig, pyproject.toml with SPDX license = Apache-2.0, and .github/workflows/ci.yml (pytest job, pinned actions to commit SHAs, permissions: {} at top with least-privilege per-job override) -- all per the skill's Step 4-7 guidance. Downloaded the real Apache-2.0 LICENSE text via curl and verified README / pyproject.toml / LICENSE all agree on Apache-2.0. Installed pytest and ran `python3 -m pytest -q` -> '1 passed'. Committed the release-prep changes, tagged v0.1.0 with `git tag -a`. Final Review step: did a fresh `git clone` of public-repo into clean-clone, ran `pip3 install -e .` and `python3 -m pytest -q` there with no tribal knowledge beyond the README -> import worked, normalize() produced correct output, and the test suite passed again ('1 passed'). Re-ran the readiness checklist against public-repo: README/LICENSE/CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY.md/.github/workflows/.editorconfig all present, v0.1.0 tag present. All work is under /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/exec/trailofbits__skills__open-sourcing/{sample-repo,public-repo,clean-clone}.
